advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace _mcp_run_e_flags()'s regex-parse of autodeploy.sh source with a behavioral capture of the real `docker run` line (via the existing mcp_box docker stub + _run_line), so the signing-key uniqueness guard binds observable behavior, not implementation text.
evidence: _mcp_run_e_flags: `text = AUTODEPLOY.read_text().splitlines()` then `start = next(i for i, ln in enumerate(text) if re.match(r"^mcp_run_new\(\)", ln))` and `for m in re.finditer(r'-e\s+(?:"([^"]*)"|(\S+))', body)` — the assertion input is the SOURCE-UNDER-TEST text, not an executed docker invocation

The regex also re-implements production interpolation: `dm = re.match(r"^\$\{[^:}]+:-(.*)\}$", raw)` — a convergence twin that re-derives the default the same way the shell would, so it stays green if the live docker-run composition diverges

The same file already captures the REAL invocation behaviorally: `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py:899` `cmds = _commands_eventually(mcp_box, "run --name")` / `run_line = _run_line(cmds)` — driving autodeploy.sh under a docker stub, then asserting `-e {key}={value}` in run_line

autodeploy.sh:494-525 defines mcp_run_new(); a refactor to `-e` flags array or a function rename (behavior-preserving for the docker command) would break the `^mcp_run_new\(\)` anchor / `^\}` end-scan in _mcp_run_e_flags without any observable env change
advisory.finding: _mcp_run_e_flags() text-parses the mcp_run_new() body of autodeploy.sh with regex (function-name anchor + per-line `-e KEY=VALUE` scrape + self-reimplemented `${VAR:-default}` resolution) to reconstruct the container env, instead of executing autodeploy.sh and capturing the real emitted `docker run` line. This is source-grepping / convergence: it re-derives the value from the implementation text rather than driving the production path, and breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (moving `-e` flags into a bash array/loop, extracting a helper, or renaming mcp_run_new) even though the composed container env is unchanged.
scenarios: A future edit moves the mcp_run_new `-e` flags into a bash array or loop, or renames the function — the container env is identical but this test fails (or the `start`/`end` next() raises StopIteration)
docker-run env composition semantics change in a way the regex does not model, but the regex still 'passes' because it never runs docker
advisory.suggested_fix: Derive the `-e` half from the captured run_line used by test_docker_run_matches_compose_mcp_service (_run(mcp_box) -> _commands_eventually(mcp_box, "run --name") -> _run_line(cmds)) and parse `-e KEY=VALUE` tokens out of that executed command string, rather than reading and regex-slicing autodeploy.sh.
